transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-18 14:00 - 14:52 UTC; Duration: 52 minutes; Attendees listed above.

Summary: Quick discovery on search ops: customer evaluating whether to run embeddings and rerank on Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Focus areas: vector DB integration patterns (hybrid vs in-service rerank), throughput and tail latency targets, embedding dimensionality and quantization, network/VPC constraints and security requirements.

00:00 Samir (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round-table intro, then we want to understand your current retrieval stack and what success looks like.
00:16 Alex (Meridian): hi all, alex here. we run a hybrid pipeline today: faiss on prem for nearest neighbor, a lucene-based re-ranker, and some custom heuristics. latency is... kinda all over the place.
00:29 Priya (Meridian): priya - ml. we embed docs with an internal bert-ish model, 768 dims, and store as float32. that's been costly, so looking at 256 dim or quantization.
00:45 Jenna (Redwood SE): great context, thanks. one clarifying q: are you planning to use an external vector DB (weaviate/pinecone/milvus) or to use Redwood to host embeddings + rerank and just push ids to your DB?
00:59 Alex: right now we push embeddings to faiss on k8s; we want to know tradeoffs. our goals: p95 < 120ms for retrieval & rerank combined for production queries, sustain 800 qps during peak, and cost under $X per 1M queries.
01:18 Samir: good, those are clear. couple of axes: 1) where embeddings are produced (client vs Redwood hosted), 2) where ANN search runs (external DB vs Redwood-managed ANN staging), and 3) whether rerank runs as a second model call (rerank on smaller candidate set) or integrated as a second-stage on the same host.
01:40 George (Meridian): security is a hard requirement for us. SOC2 yes, also SAML/SSO, and we need VPC peering for Dedicated/Private. can you do KMS/HSM for key management?
01:55 Marco (Redwood): yes to SOC2 and SSO; we support KMS integrations and HSM for Private deployments. Dedicated gives VPC peering and private subnets; Hosted can be configured with VPC egress but private on-prem is also an option.
02:12 Priya: we also need audit logs for embedding writes and must be able to trace vectors back to document IDs for debugging.
02:25 Jenna: action: we can include token-level logs for inference requests and a structured write-audit for embedding ops; we'll share how that looks in the security pack.
02:40 Alex: on the technical side, our current faiss cluster is sharded by doc_id hash, and we do fanout to 8 shards. rereank is a BERT crossencoder that scores top-100 from ANN. wondering if it's better to: A) increase ANN accuracy (bigger dim, no quant) so rerank can be cheaper; B) keep low-dim+quant and rely on stronger rerank; or C) use Redwood's built-in hybrid rerank that layers lightweight scorer in-service.
03:10 Jenna: those are classic tradeoffs. quantization reduces memory and increases throughput but can hurt recall. we typically recommend a hybrid: use 256-d or 384-d quantized for first-pass ANN, then run a smaller cross-encoder or a distilled reranker on top for precision. that lets you reduce ANN fanout and keep tail-latency SLOs.
03:35 Priya: what about KV cache / prefix cache to speed up repeated queries? we have lots of similar user queries.
03:44 Marco: Redwood supports automatic prefix/KV caching for streaming and generation; for embeddings/ANN we do request-level caching and can surface cold/warm hit metrics. if your workload has high repeat rate we can save a lot on token cost and latency.
03:58 Alex: and throughput: do you have reference numbers for 256-d vs 512-d on dedicated GPUs? we need sustained 800 qps at p95 120ms.
04:08 Jenna: rough ballpark for Dedicated with optimized kernels: 256-d quantized ANN lookup + lightweight rerank (cross-encoder latency ~12-25ms on a single GPU if batched properly) could hit 800 qps with sharded workers and continuous batching. exact numbers depend on model, sequence len, and batching policy. we'll need to run a benchmark with your actual model and queries.
04:31 Priya: our reranker is heavy; currently 80ms p50 and bad p95. can Redwood do per-route autoscaling for that? we don't want to overprovision.
04:42 Marco: yes, Dedicated supports per-route autoscaling with reserved capacity and burst pools; you can pin capacity for rerank routes and have automatic spillover to a lower-cost variant. also canary rollouts if you change models.
04:58 George: are there options for local rerank near the DB to avoid cross-region latency if we run faiss on-prem?
05:08 Jenna: two patterns: 1) colocate ANN and rerank in private deployment/on-prem so traffic is local; 2) use a lightweight ANN in Redwood and only send ids or small payloads back to your DB for final doc fetch. For hybrid search we sometimes run an edge ANN with periodic sync to central FAISS.
05:32 Alex: ok. another question: index stitching and sharding - we currently rebalance shards offline and it causes query spikes. can Redwood help with online re-sharding or rolling rebuilds?
05:48 Marco: our Dedicated orchestrator supports rolling index rebuilds with warmup periods and can route traffic away from shards under rebuild. there's also a feature to pre-warm caches after rebuild so you don't see the cold-start spike.
06:05 Priya: what about embedding dimensionality? we want to go from 768 -> 256 or 384. what's the typical retrieval quality delta, and do you have guidance on model distillation vs PCA vs quantization?
06:18 Jenna: distillation to a smaller model typically preserves semantic quality better than naive PCA. quantization (8-bit/4-bit) is complementary. the platform can host your distilled model or we can host a community distill variant. we'll include eval guidance and provide A/B test harness to measure MRR/NDCG on your eval set.
06:38 Alex: sounds good. do you support hybrid text+vector rerank where we combine BM25 score with vector similarity? we rely on a lexical signal for some docs.
06:50 Samir: yes, Redwood supports hybrid scoring pipelines; you can either fuse signals in your client or use our reranker to accept lexical features + vector features and produce final score. Many customers send BM25 or TFIDF features along with candidates.
07:07 George: latency and network - if we go Dedicated in a VPC, what's the egress pattern? do requests from our app go directly into the VPC or proxied through Redwood control plane?
07:20 Marco: data path option: customer traffic can route directly to Dedicated instances in your VPC. control plane calls are separate; inference traffic stays within the private network. for Hosted we do secure links but there's egress to Redwood infra. we'll share a diagram.
07:35 Priya: billing question: is billing usage-based only or do you do committed capacity for Dedicated?
07:42 Samir: Hosted is usage-based. Dedicated supports reserved monthly commits with overage pricing and burst pool options. Private deployments often involve a platform fee + support. we'll provide sample numbers.
07:56 Alex: ok let's talk benchmarks and the pilot. we'd like a 48-hour run: 2M doc vectors, 512-d and 256-d variants, 100k unique queries replayed for realistic qps spike patterns. can Redwood run this on Dedicated?
08:12 Jenna: yes, we can spin up a Dedicated pilot for benchmarking. we'll need your sample embeddings and query traces. we'll share a template.
08:20 Priya: also need to check compliance: we can't send PHI outside certain networks; how do Private deployments work for air-gapped needs?
08:31 Marco: Private on-prem can be deployed air-gapped with local control plane; we support HSM/KMS and SOC2 + addtl compliance packages. we'll enumerate the options in the security pack.
08:45 Samir: quick note on rerank architecture options we recommend: 1) two-stage: ANN candidate generation (256-384 quantized) -> cross-encoder rerank on top-K; 2) single-model hybrid scorer using a distilled cross-encoder that accepts embeddings and lexical features; 3) embedding+rerank co-located in Dedicated to cut network hop for latency-sensitive traffic.
09:12 Alex: what's the operational burden of running Dedicated vs Hosted? our infra team prefers Managed but wants control.
09:22 Marco: Dedicated hits a sweet spot: managed infra with reserved capacity, but VPC and private subnets give you network control. you still get Redwood console, tracing, token-level breakdowns, and rollout controls. Private gives max control but more ops involvement.
09:36 Priya: any gotchas with quantization and recall? we've seen some drop at tail queries for edge cases.
09:44 Jenna: quantify with eval sets; often 4-bit quant with per-channel scale yields small quality loss for dense retrieval if you also rerank. We recommend re-eval on your dev holdout and iterative quant+retrain.
09:59 Alex: competitors we've looked at: pinecone for simplicity, weaviate for on-prem-ish, milvus for OSS. how is Redwood different?
10:08 Samir: we position as runtime + ops: you get high-throughput optimized kernels, unified API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, first-class rollouts, and built-in rerank patterns. plus the observability for per-route economics.
10:24 George: ok. curious about cost math: if we do 2-stage with Dedicated for ANN and Hosted for rerank, is that odd?
10:33 Marco: you can mix variants; the router can fall back to Hosted rerank if Dedicated capacity is drained. But cross-region hops cost latency; prefer co-location if p95 SLO tight.
10:48 Priya: final question - do you support model version pinning and canary for rerank models?
10:56 Jenna: yes, we support model pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic rollback on quality regression tied to prompt sets or rerank evals.
11:08 Samir: great - recap of next steps: we'll send benchmark template + security docs; customer to upload sample vectors and query trace; schedule SE deep dive for rerank specifics week of 1/25. any other questions?
11:25 Alex: no, thanks — excited to see the benchmark numbers.
11:31 Priya: thanks all.
11:34 Meeting end.

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker labels were fuzzy (Speaker 2 appears) and there are some minor word swaps (Pinecone transcribed as Pinecon in one segment). The transcript preserves hesitations and overlapping talk in places.
